newsitem.title: USA: Niagara Mohawk to sell half of subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: Niagara Mohawk to sell half of subsidiary.

text.p: Niagara Mohawk Power Corp said Wednesday it agreed in principle to sell 50 percent of Canadian Niagara Power to Fortis Inc for undisclosed terms.
Canadian Niagara Power is currently owned by Opinac Energy, a Niagara Mohawk subsidiary. Niagara Mohawk said the transaction is expected to close shortly.

"Partnership with a strong Canadian company such as Fortis will position Canadian Niagara Power to compete and expand as Ontario transitions to a competitive electricity marketplace," said Niagara Mohawk.

Canadian Niagara Power generates 650,000 megawatt-hours of electricity annually. It transmits and distributes electricity to some 13,500 customers in the town of Fort Erie, Ontario, and sells electricity to the City of Cornwall.

The utility also owns a wind farm, located in Cowley Ridge, Alberta, which sells electricity to Trans Alta Utilities Corp. Canadian Niagara Power has been in continuous operation since the late 19th century and owns and operates the Rankine Generating Station located on the Niagara River, just above Niagara Falls.
